result.rationale: The diff sets `destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither eventType nor organizerUser has one, then later executes `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If it's null, the optional chaining makes the push a no-op, so team hosts' destination calendars collected in `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded — collective team events would not be created on team hosts' calendars. Mechanism is directly verifiable in the diff.

record.issue_text: Team hosts' destination calendars are silently dropped when organizer/eventType have none: evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) is a no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null, discarding collected host calendars without warning

adjudication.rationale:
In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when both `eventType.destinationCalendar` and `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` are falsy:
```ts
destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar
  ? [eventType.destinationCalendar]
  : organizerUser.destinationCalendar
  ? [organizerUser.destinationCalendar]
  : null,
```
Later, for COLLECTIVE team events, host calendars are collected into `teamDestinationCalendars`, but they are only appended via an optional-chained push:
```ts
if (isTeamEventType && eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE") {
  evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);
}
```
If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, this is a no-op, so the collected team hosts’ destination calendars are silently dropped. This is a correctness/data-loss behavior directly implied by the diff.
